title: Automated batching proposals with secure apply and rollback workflow
creator: Aisha Nand
description: Build an end-to-end flow that turns runtime instrumentation into concrete batching/caching configuration proposals, and safely applies or rolls back those proposals under RBAC and auditable change management. The system should produce human-reviewable proposals, allow policy-driven automatic apply for low-risk changes, require multi-step approval for higher-risk changes, record an immutable audit trail, and support immediate automated rollback if an adverse signal is detected.
background: We already generate recommendations from the batching advisor prototype, but there is no safe, compliant path to apply those changes to Dedicated/Private runtime configs. Teams want predictable cost wins without compromising reliability or compliance. This ticket unifies proposal generation, risk classification, approval gates, apply/rollback mechanics, and forensic logging.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal generator emits JSON proposals that include: model id, route, suggested batch_size, kv_cache_policy, expected QPS impact, estimated cost delta, and risk score
RBAC-enforced apply endpoint that accepts proposals and validates user or service principal permissions before execution
Two-tier approval flow: auto-apply for low-risk proposals (per policy); manual approval required for medium/high-risk proposals
Immutable audit logs for every step (proposal, approval, apply, rollback) stored in customer-configurable retention store with tamper-evidence metadata
Rollback triggers: latency SLO breach, error-rate spike, or custom metric threshold — rollback must be executable within 60s of trigger
End-to-end integration tests covering propose -> approve -> apply -> rollback on a local test cluster and in staging environment
success_metrics: Reduce per-token cost by >= 6% in controlled experiments where proposals were applied
<= 3 incidents / quarter caused by automated applies across Dedicated clusters
Audit log completeness: 100% of proposal lifecycle events present in logs for 90-day window
Mean time to rollback after trigger <= 90s in staging
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Proposal generator in staging; Phase 2: Read-only proposals surfaced in Console; Phase 3: Enable auto-apply for a small sandbox customer under a feature flag; Phase 4: Gradual ramp with monitoring and rollback policies; Phase 5: GA with configurable enterprise policies and retention settings
test_plan: Unit tests for proposal serializer and risk classifier
Integration test that runs a simulated traffic profile, applies a low-risk change, verifies cost and latency signals
Chaos test that simulates backend NVidia mem pressure and ensures rollback triggers
Audit log tamper test using stored hashes
implementation_notes: Use existing batching-advisor model but normalize output schema to canonical proposal v2
Attach a deterministic fingerprints (sha256) to proposals so rollback can pin to the exact applied change
Store audit events in append-only blob with hashed linking for tamper evidence; expose signed attestations for enterprise customers
Leverage RBAC service (authz) to enforce who/which service principal can auto-apply or require approval
Design the apply API to run in a transaction-like manner: validate -> stage -> swap -> post-check -> commit/rollback
security_considerations: Attestation required for any auto-apply path: service principal must present attestation token and be in allowlist
Ensure proposal payloads are sanitized and validated to prevent config injection
Encrypt audit blobs at rest with customer KMS where configured
Restrict rollback execution to the same policy boundary that performed the apply or to platform ops with 'force-rollback' justification
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike completed: prototype proposal schema and risk classifier. Low-risk heuristics defined.
2026-03-02: Security review kickoff. Initial RBAC model proposed (role: proposer, approver, auditor, operator).
2026-03-05: Eng sync: prefer append-only audit store over SQL for simpler tamper-evidence. Need KMS integration design.
Trade-offs: aggressive auto-apply increases cost savings but raises incident risk. We'll start conservative and expand policy set.
Open question: whether to allow cross-customer automated apply in multi-tenant runtime; default will be per-customer only.
